data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is an under-powered measurement artifact: the test constrains only when its constraint is load-bearing in the installation path, and the distribution is the small-sample fingerprint of one repository, one author, one week \u2014 no structural condition can be inferred beyond the ritual's local ordering.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a larger mutation sample (e.g., 100+ per module) preserves the 3/26 ratio, then the effect is not small-sample noise.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same author's other repositories show the same 3-of-26 pattern, then it is authorial style, not local chance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the compile.py 1/9 loss is reproducible across multiple independent mutation sets, then it is a stable hole, not a sampling artifact.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the record contains a control group without installation, and the 3-of-26 disappears, then the installation ritual is confirmed as the active ingredient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The caveat in the record is explicit: one repository, one author, one week, mutations proposed by models that had read the acceptance record. The 4/4 to 6/7 spread across ordinarily-guarded modules is the expected variance when each module's guard coverage is independent and the sample size is 9 mutations in compile.py.
